lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: So where are all the beautiful people, Hermes — the men, the women? Give me the tour. I'm new.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: I don't really have time, Menippus. But — look over there, to the right. That's where Hyacinthus is, and Narcissus, and Nireus, and Achilles, and Tyro, and Helen, and Leda — all the classic beauties, basically.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: All I see is bones. Skulls stripped of their flesh. Mostly identical.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Well, those are the bones every poet swoons over. The ones you appear to be unimpressed by.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Show me Helen, anyway. I'd never pick her out on my own.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: [pause] This is what they filled a thousand ships for? Out of all of Greece? This is what so many Greeks and barbarians died over, and so many cities were leveled for?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Ah, but you didn't see the woman alive, Menippus. If you had, you'd have said the same as Homer — no shame in suffering long years for a woman like that. Look — dried flowers, when they've lost their color, obviously they look like nothing. But while they're in bloom, while they've still got their hue — they're the loveliest thing there is.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Then that's what amazes me, Hermes — that the Achaeans didn't grasp they were sweating and dying over something so short-lived. Something that wilts that easily.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: [sighs] I don't have time to philosophize with you, Menippus. So — pick a spot, wherever you like, lie down, settle in. I've got the rest of the dead to collect.
